body: This seems to be a bug in the way we handle bots in field names.

> This seems to be a bug in the way we handle bots in field names.

We allow bots in field names??!?

This looks like it might be related to a discussion over on discuss from last week:

https://discuss.elastic.co/t/name-cannot-be-empty-string-error-if-field-name-starts-with/66808/2
Something which is interesting for me, `foo.` "works" as a field name. I get a mapping with `foo` (no dot) as a field name. Expected?

I know this bug has been open for a while, but I am looking more into it again. I was looking at the discussion here: [https://discuss.elastic.co/t/name-cannot-be-empty-string-error-if-field-name-starts-with/66808/2](https://discuss.elastic.co/t/name-cannot-be-empty-string-error-if-field-name-starts-with/66808/2) based on @MaineC 's comment. I am getting conflicting information: some are saying it's a bug and others are saying it's just a documentation problem. Can some Elasticsearch developers advise me where they are on this issue?
@danlevy1 It's not a bug that a field may not be called `.`. It is a bug that we throw an AOOB exception - we should return a more meaningful exception.
